description: Hand-worked cases for oracles/pixel_sampler.py (oracle rule 5). A 5-slice axial DICOM stack (8 x 8, PixelSpacing [2, 3]: 2 mm between rows, 3 mm between columns; IPP_k = (-10, -20, 5k); IOP (1,0,0, 0,1,0)) and a NIfTI built by hand from it. Five slices, not three: under the plan 3.6 mirror rule the middle slice of an odd stack mirrors onto itself and is never kept, so a 3-slice stack could not meet the 3-slice spread rule.
work: Pixel (r, c, k): LPS P = (-10 + 3c, -20 + 2r, 5k), so RAS = (10 - 3c, 20 - 2r, 5k). The affine maps voxel (i, j, k) to RAS (10 - 3i, 20 - 2j, 5k), so (i, j, k) = (c, r, k) and the NIfTI array is nifti[i, j, k] = dicom_k[r = j, c = i].

cases.work: dataobj returns 2*stored + 10; the sampler recovers stored = (value - 10) / 2

cases.nifti: affine shifted by half a voxel along i
cases.work: every voxel index is off by 0.5: 'off grid'

cases.nifti: 4D, two volumes stored in swapped order
cases.work: every sample of volume 0 is found at volume 1 and the reverse
axis 1 of the NIfTI carries the DICOM row index (j = r), so flipping it reverses the row order; the DICOM marks GE epi_pepolar mode 1 (owner decision at G1)
the same row reversal in a forward (mode 0) pepolar series is not explained
